claim: On the current source and audited McWilliams established-base footing, the real native Zone Manager owner can expose a stable faction-scoped zone, apply one advertised enable or disable action, reject a stale or unavailable control without mutation, and retain the resulting state through native save, process replacement, and relaunch.
material_proof: An independent current-source run enters through world.zone_manager, records the native Zone Manager descriptor and receipt, observes exact stable zone identity/faction/enabled/revision before and after one native mutation, records a rejected control with unchanged state, then verifies the same saved state after native exit and relaunch with accepted cleanup and a bounded feel observation.
material_contradiction: World does not enter the native Zone Manager owner
the action applies to a different zone or stale revision
native save/relaunch loses the observed state
physical input, direct state mutation, setup, or a semantic acceptance alone is credited as behavior
already_accepted_evidence: R-026 established-base audit is readiness only.
Zone identity/revision and semantic owner unit tests are implementation evidence only.
current_uncertainty: The fixture's currently active zone and save lifecycle must be independently observed; fixture setup has zero feature credit.
forbidden_shortcuts: crediting startup or descriptor publication as gameplay behavior
honest_stop_conditions: missing current binding or authorization before launch
after launch preserve the first owner, receipt, state, or persistence divergence while retaining unaffected controls
